title: The CSS Box Model
description: Master the fundamental layers of every HTML box: content area, padding, border, and margin; calculate dimensions and understand box-sizing: border-box.

objectives.statement: Configure the 4 layers of the CSS Box Model: content area, padding, border, and margin.
Calculate total element dimensions and apply box-sizing: border-box for predictable layouts.

content.title: Every Element is a Box
content.hook: In web layout, everything you see is a rectangular box. Mastering the 4 layers of that box is the single most important milestone in CSS layout.
content.context: From the inside out: 1. Content (text/images), 2. Padding (space inside the border), 3. Border (the frame line), 4. Margin (space outside the border pushing neighbors away).
goals: Differentiate internal padding from external margin.
Calculate total rendered element width and height.
Apply `box-sizing: border-box` to prevent size calculation headaches.

content.title: The Concentric Layers of the Box Model
content.description: Concentric boxes: Content Area (center) surrounded by Padding (light blue), Border (solid dark line), and Margin (outer orange buffer).

content.prompt: An element has default `box-sizing: content-box` with `width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid black; margin: 15px;`. What is the total rendered width occupied by the element on screen (border-to-border)?
options: 200px (padding and border sit inside the width)
250px (200 content + 20 left padding + 20 right padding + 5 left border + 5 right border)

validation.expected: 250px (200 content + 20 left padding + 20 right padding + 5 left border + 5 right border)

feedback.correct: Spot on! Under default `content-box`, `width` only sets the content area. Total border-to-border rendered width = 200 + 20(left pad) + 20(right pad) + 5(left border) + 5(right border) = 250px.
feedback.incorrect: Remember the `content-box` formula: Total rendered width = width + padding-left + padding-right + border-left + border-right = 200 + 40 + 10 = 250px.

content.title: Construct a Predictable Box Card
content.prompt:
Style the `.card` element:
1. Set `box-sizing: border-box` and `width: 300px`.
2. Add `padding: 24px` inside the card.
3. Add a `border: 2px solid #cbd5e1`.
4. Add `margin-bottom: 20px` to create breathing room below.
content.starterCode:
Box Model Card

Padding breathes inside; margin pushes outside.

feedback.correct: Outstanding! With `box-sizing: border-box`, your 300px card stays exactly 300px wide regardless of padding and border widths.
feedback.incorrect: Check your properties: set `box-sizing: border-box`, `width: 300px`, `padding: 24px`, `border: 2px solid #cbd5e1`, and `margin-bottom: 20px`.

hints.content: Add `box-sizing: border-box; width: 300px; padding: 24px;` inside the `.card` selector.

content.prompt: Why do almost all modern CSS resets apply `*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }` across the entire document?

feedback.correct: Great analysis! Border-box ensures that declared `width` includes padding and borders, making mathematical layout calculations intuitive and preventing unwanted horizontal overflow.
feedback.incorrect: Think about how border-box simplifies width calculations and prevents containers from expanding when adding padding.

content.title: Key Takeaways: CSS Box Model
takeaways: Every element is composed of Content, Padding, Border, and Margin.
Padding adds internal breathing room between content and border.
Margin creates external spacing pushing sibling and parent elements away.
box-sizing: border-box incorporates padding and border into the specified width/height.
Universal border-box resets eliminate unexpected overflow.
